sn36.12:1.1: “Bhikkhus, just as various winds blow in the sky:
sn36.12:1.2: winds from the east, winds from the west, winds from the north, winds from the south, dusty winds and dustless winds, cold winds and hot winds, mild winds and strong winds;
sn36.12:1.3: so too, various feelings arise in this body: pleasant feeling arises, painful feeling arises, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises.”
sn36.12:2.2: Blow back and forth across the sky,
sn36.12:3.3: Those that are strong and others mild—
sn36.12:3.4: Winds of many kinds that blow;
sn36.12:4.1: So in this very body here
sn36.12:4.4: And those neither painful nor pleasant.
sn36.12:5.1: But when a bhikkhu who is ardent
sn36.12:5.3: Then that wise man fully understands
sn36.12:6.2: He is taintless in this very life.
sn36.12:6.4:
with the body’s breakup,
The knowledge-master cannot be reckoned.
